Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

18:2156-1962 



Indian Standard 

CODE FOR PACKING 
RAW WOOL FOR EXPORT 

0. FOREWORD 



0,1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the 
Indian Standards Institution on 24 August 1962, 
after the draft finalized by tht: Woo! Sectional 
Committee had been approved by the Textile 
Division Council* 

0.2 The object of packing raw wool is to bring 
it to a convenient form for the purpose of trans- 
port and to ensure that the material arrives in 
sound condition at destination, 

0-3 The method of packing raw wool pre* 



scribed in this standard is applicable only when 
bales are made in a press comprising a half ( or 
kutcha ) press and a full ( or pucca ) press* 

0,4 Wherever a reference to any Indian Stand- 
ard appears in this code, it shall be taken as a 
reference to the latest version of the standard. 



0*5 Metric system has been adopted in India 
and all quantities and dimensions in this 
standard have been given in this system. 



1. SCOPE 

1,1 This code prescribes the method of packing 
raw wool for export purposes, 

tJZ The method may also be used in case the 
wool is to be transported over internal water- 
ways or on land where the distance is great, 
time taken in transit is considerable, climatic 
conditions are variable, or the goods are to be 
frequently unloaded and reloaded during 
transit, 

2* PACKING PROCEDURE 

2*1 Weigh the quantity of wool required to form 
a bale* ( The weight of a bale shall be not less 
than 100 kg nor more than 200 kg^ } Place one 
piece of medium weight new hessian of suitable 
size and conforming to the requirements of 
Table I, at the bottom of the box of the 
half press to form the bottom layer to cover the 
bale* Fill the box with wool previously weighed* 
Attach another piece of hessian of similar 
quality under the top portion of the half press 
to form the top layer to cover the bale. The 
si^e of this piece of hessian shall be such that 
the three sides ( top and the other two sides ) of 
the bale are covered when the bale is fully 
pressed* Operate the press till the bale is half 



pressed- Transfer the half pressed bale to the 
full press* Cover the two ends of the bale with 
pieces of hessian of similar quality and press 
the bale to the optimum size. While the bale 
is stiU under pressure, bind it at right angle to 
its length with new medium grade 0'90 mm 
( 20 SWG ) thick and minimum 16 mm wide flat 
steel strips (or hoops ) conforming to the appli- 
cable requirements of IS : 1029-1956 Specifica* 
tion for Hot Rolled Steel Strips (Baling), so 
that: 

a) the strips nearest to the tdgcs of the bale 
are approximately 13 cm away from the 
respective edges of the balc> 

b) the other strips are also positioned at 
approximately 13 cm from each other and 
are equally spaced, and 

c) the strips are drawn taut and the loose 
ends folded and pushed under the strips. 

Stitch with 3-ply jute twinc^ the pieces of hessian 
used for covering the two ends of the bale to the 
hessian used for covering the sides, 

3, MARKING 

3,1 A label, giving the necessary information 
required by the buyer or by the law in force, 
shall be attached to each bale.
